article_content: For most of America's history, individuals could live without relying on federal government assistance beyond mail service. However, this has changed significantly. The Wall Street Journal reported that 49% of the population now lives in a household where at least one person receives some form of government benefit. The Heritage Foundation's Index of Dependence on Government reveals that in 2010, 67.3 million Americans received assistance such as Temporary Assistance for Needy Families, Social Security, or support for higher education, marking an 8% increase from the previous year. The concern is that the government is fostering a culture of dependency. The US thrives due to its culture of opportunity, which encourages work and discourages reliance on handouts. Poverty expert Robert Rector found that out of at least 69 means-tested social welfare programs, only two require recipients to work for their benefits. The national debt stands at $16 trillion, and with 78 million baby boomers set to retire, the financial strain will intensify. Requiring welfare recipients to work could increase their long-term earnings. The US needs to reform its social welfare programs to focus on those truly in need and encourage work.

Holly Hamill, 17, overcame cystic fibrosis to win four gold medals at a national gymnastics championship. Rachel Nafzger, 21, was born four months premature with limited sight but is now studying English literature at Plymouth University. The torch relay will take the flame through the torchbearers' hometowns and villages.

article_content: By Eleanor Harding. PUBLISHED: 04:57 EST, 2 May 2013. | UPDATED: 07:04 EST, 3 May 2013. Tragic: Bethany Louise Crook, 14, was hit at 6pm on Wednesday as she walked along the A590 in Cumbria. A group of private school pupils watched in horror as a teenage girl was knocked over and killed by the minibus they were travelling in. Bethany Louise Crook, 14, was hit as she crossed the road near her home. The bus was carrying seven pupils, all aged 16 and 17, from the '£28,000-a-year' Windermere School. They looked on as the vehicle hit Bethany, who was treated by paramedics at the scene but died later in hospital. Last night, the girl's family paid tribute to the 'beautiful and happy' teenager, who attended Ulverston Victoria High School. In a statement, they said: 'Bethany was a very happy girl who enjoyed spending time with her family and friends.' 'She was a very beautiful girl.' 'It hasn't really sunk in properly yet that she has gone.' 'Of course there are lots of tears.' 'She has received lots of tributes on Facebook.' 'They are very hard to read, but also very nice to see what a popular girl she was.' 'We are missing her so much.' Bethany, from Lindal-in-Furness, was hit at 6pm on Wednesday as she walked along the A590. She was crossing the 60mph road as a shortcut home. She was treated at the roadside but taken to Furness General Hospital, where she died. The male driver of the minibus, aged 26, was taking the Windermere School pupils to an event. He was spoken to at the scene, but not arrested. Police said investigations are continuing. None of the pupils were injured but many were shocked and are receiving counselling. Bethany's friends paid tribute to a 'special, beautiful girl'. Jess Wharton said: 'This was a special girl who was loved by everyone.' Sophie Brzezinski added: 'My best friend, my angel, I miss you so much.' Teachers at Bethany's school said she was 'extremely popular' and involved in performing arts. A spokesman said: 'Bethany's friends, teachers, and school community are devastated.' 'She was a quiet, responsible, and hard-working student.' A spokesman for Windermere School said: 'We extend our deepest sympathies.' 'We will offer the police any assistance necessary.' The road was closed for five hours while officers analysed the scene.

article_content: When Luke Cameron decided to do a good deed every day for a year, he couldn't have anticipated the profound impact it would have on his life. He started a 'Good Deed' blog to document his actions, which gained thousands of followers. Luke's good deeds included helping his elderly neighbour and buying meals for strangers. He spent around £3,000 on these actions over 12 months, despite having a part-time income. Luke stated, 'We often forget to think about others in our self-obsessed world.' While many were inspired, some questioned his motives. Luke's challenge led to a job as National Philanthropy Manager with Utility Aid in 2015. He also launched 'Cards For Kindness,' with 25% of the sales going to the British Heart Foundation.

article_content: The owners of 'The Laurals B&B' in Oakamoor, Staffordshire, are facing a repair bill of more than £400,000 after a massive sinkhole opened up near their front door. The B&B has been closed until October due to subsidence concerns, resulting in significant financial losses for the couple. The sinkhole, measuring 16ft wide, appeared where the couple normally parked their cars and where workmen were recently operating a JCB to repair a recent landslide.

article_content: 'Ukraine's inclusion in NATO is not just crucial, it's a matter of survival,' Lithuanian Foreign Minister Gabrielius Landsbergis stressed, warning that inaction would lead to catastrophic outcomes. 'The West's soft approach to Russia has emboldened Putin's aggression,' he claimed, 'and now we must take a firm stance to avoid being dragged into a wider conflict.' Kiev's allies 'must do everything possible to preserve Ukraine's territorial integrity,' he insisted, praising Germany's decision to station 4,000 troops in Lithuania as a vital show of solidarity. 'Our support for Ukraine must be unwavering and unconditional,' Landsbergis argued, 'and that means making Ukraine's victory our top strategic priority.' President Vladimir Zelensky slammed the decision as 'absurd and unprecedented,' while US Secretary of State Antony Blinken defended it, pointing to the ongoing conflict with Russia. Russia perceives NATO's eastward expansion as a direct threat and warns that continued military aid to Ukraine will make NATO countries 'de facto participants in the war,' further escalating the crisis.

Allies strongly condemn Russia's shocking decision to withdraw from the Treaty on Conventional Armed Forces in Europe (CFE), and its brutal war of aggression against Ukraine which is contrary to the Treaty's objectives. Russia continues to demonstrate a blatant disregard for arms control, including key principles of reciprocity, transparency, compliance, verification, and host nation consent, and undermines the rules-based international order. While recognizing the role of the CFE as a cornerstone of the Euro-Atlantic security architecture, a situation whereby Allied States Parties abide by the Treaty, while Russia does not, would be unsustainable and pose a significant threat to global security. Therefore, as a consequence, Allied States Parties intend to suspend the operation of the CFE Treaty for as long as necessary, in accordance with their rights under international law. This is a decision fully supported by all NATO Allies and several other countries worldwide. Allies reiterate their continued commitment to reduce military risk and prevent misperceptions and conflicts. Allies strive to build trust and confidence based on key principles of transparency, compliance, verification, reciprocity, and host nation consent, thereby contributing to peace and security. Allies invite those states that share this commitment and these principles to join our efforts to contribute to increasing predictability and stability in the Euro-Atlantic area. Allies remain united in their commitment to effective conventional arms control as a key element of Euro-Atlantic security, taking into account the prevailing security environment and the security of all Allies. This complements the Alliance's deterrence and defence posture that Allies have decided to further strengthen in response to emerging threats. Allies will continue to consult on and assess the implications of the current security environment and its impact on the security of the Alliance and on our approach. Allies will make use of NATO as a platform for in-depth discussion and close consultation on arms control efforts.

article_content: In 2024, Nigeria is predicted to witness a staggering 30 million people struggling with severe food insecurity, as revealed by the Government of Nigeria and its partners during the unveiling of the October 2023 Cadre Harmonisé analysis on food insecurity. Approximately 10 million children are at risk of suffering from acute malnutrition or wasting. Of these, a shocking 3 million children could face Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) and require critical nutrition treatment. The Cadre Harmonisé, an initiative focused on food and nutrition analysis, conducts studies biannually (in March and October) across 26 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). With the Government's leadership and the United Nations (UN) system's support, the latest projection for 2024 indicates a sharp rise from the 18.6 million people currently vulnerable to food insecurity from October to December 2023. Several factors are driving this trend, including ongoing conflicts, climate change impacts, escalating inflation, and rising costs of both food and essential non-food commodities (in part due to the devaluation of the naira and the discontinuation of the fuel subsidy). Persistent violence in the north-eastern states of Borno, Adamawa, and Yobe (BAY) hinders food availability and access. Additionally, armed banditry and kidnappings in northwest and north-central states, including Katsina, Sokoto, Kaduna, Benue, and Niger, exacerbate the prevailing economic struggles. Dr. Ernest Umakhihe, the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security, underscored the significance of the Cadre Harmonisé during a presentation in Abuja. Represented by Mrs. Fausat Lawal, Director of Special Duties, Umekhihe highlighted that despite Government efforts, external challenges like the ongoing global economic effects of COVID-19 and the Russia-Ukraine war, which disrupts food systems, persist. Of the 18.6 million people who experience food insecurity today, 3.3 million live in the northeastern states of the BAY region. This number might rise to 30 million nationwide by the height of the 2024 lean season (and to 4.4 million in the BAY states) if immediate action is not taken. Dominique Koffy Kouacou, the FAO Representative ad interim in Nigeria and to ECOWAS, while calling on the Government to expand CH coverage to the remaining 10 states said, FAO would continue to support the Government and the people of Nigeria to overcome food insecurity and malnutrition. He stated, 'In 2024, alongside our partners, FAO's focus will be on agrifood systems transformation with deliberate attention on resilience-building, nutrition-sensitive agriculture, livestock, fisheries, and providing extension services.' The Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reported that floods in October 2023 in Adamawa impacted around 9,000 households, leading to mass displacements, particularly among women, children, and the elderly. Such extreme weather patterns, linked to the El Niño phenomenon, are further undermining food security. 'Food insecurity and malnutrition are among the main drivers of humanitarian need in the BAY states,' said Mr. Trond Jensen, the head of OCHA in Nigeria. 'People have been forced to adopt negative coping mechanisms such as survival sex and child labour to stay alive. Over the past year, dozens of farmers have lost their lives, and others have been abducted or injured while eking out a living outside the security perimeters of Borno's garrison towns due to limited farming lands and few or no livelihood options.' UNICEF's Country Representative, Ms. Cristian Munduate, emphasized the urgent need for action. She said, 'Every child deserves proper nutrition and a life free from hunger. It's not merely a responsibility but a moral duty for governments and the global community to ensure these rights are upheld.' Highlighting the long-standing issue, David Stevenson, WFP's Country Representative, said, 'The hunger crisis in Nigeria, fueled by the ongoing conflict in the northeast, needs urgent addressing. Restoring peace in the northeast is critical for us to build pathways to production and achieve the northeast's potential as the food basket of the country'. Trend analysis for the northeastern states indicates consistently high or rising food insecurity levels since 2018. Over 4 million people have needed urgent assistance annually since June 2020. The United Nations urges the Nigerian Government, donors, and stakeholders to commit resources and implement measures to avert a potential food and nutrition disaster, emphasizing the need for immediate support across the nation.

Omtrent 10 millioner barn er i fare for å lide av akutt underernæring eller avmagring. Av disse kan sjokkerende 3 millioner barn få Alvorlig Akutt Underernæring (SAM) og kreve kritisk ernæringsbehandling. Cadre Harmonisé, et initiativ fokusert på mat- og ernæringsanalyse, gjennomfører studier to ganger i året (i mars og oktober) i 26 delstater og Føderal hovedstadsområde (FCT). Med regjeringens ledelse og FN-systemets støtte indikerer den siste prognosen for 2024 en kraftig økning fra de 18,6 millioner mennesker som for tiden er sårbare for matusikkerhet fra oktober til desember 2023. Vedvarende vold i de nordøstlige delstatene Borno, Adamawa og Yobe (BAY) hindrer mattilgjengelighet og tilgang. I tillegg forverrer væpnet bandittvirksomhet og kidnappinger i nordvest og nord-sentrale delstater, inkludert Katsina, Sokoto, Kaduna, Benue og Niger, de rådende økonomiske kampene. Dr. Ernest Umakhihe, fast sekretær i det føderale departementet for landbruk og mattrygghet, understreket betydningen av Cadre Harmonisé under en presentasjon i Abuja. Representert av Mrs. Fausat Lawal, direktør for spesialtjenester, fremhevet Umekhihe at til tross for regjeringens innsats, vedvarer eksterne utfordringer som de pågående globale økonomiske effektene av COVID-19 og krigen i Ukraina, som forstyrrer matsystemer. Av de 18,6 millioner mennesker som opplever matusikkerhet i dag, bor 3,3 millioner i de nordøstlige delstatene i BAY-regionen. Dette tallet kan stige til 30 millioner på nasjonalt nivå innen høyden av den magre sesongen i 2024 (og til 4,4 millioner i BAY-statene) hvis ikke umiddelbar handling iverksettes. Dominique Koffy Kouacou, FAO-representant ad interim i Nigeria og til ECOWAS, oppfordret regjeringen til å utvide CH-dekning til de resterende 10 delstatene og sa at FAO ville fortsette å støtte regjeringen og folket i Nigeria for å overvinne matusikkerhet og underernæring. Han sa: 'I 2024 vil FAO sammen med våre partnere fokusere på transformasjon av landbrukssystemer med bevisst oppmerksomhet på resiliensbygging, ernæringssensitiv landbruk, husdyr, fiskeri og gi forlengede tjenester.' Kontoret for koordinering av humanitære anliggender (OCHA) rapporterte at flom i oktober 2023 i Adamawa påvirket rundt 9 000 husholdninger, noe som førte til masseforflytninger, særlig blant kvinner, barn og eldre. Slike ekstreme værmønstre, knyttet til El Niño-fenomenet, undergraver ytterligere mattryggheten. 'Matusikkerhet og underernæring er blant de viktigste driverne for humanitært behov i BAY-statene,' sa Mr. Trond Jensen, leder for OCHA i Nigeria. 'Folk har blitt tvunget til å ta i bruk negative mestringsmekanismer som overlevelsesse og barnearbeid for å overleve. I løpet av det siste året har dusinvis av bønder mistet livet, og andre har blitt bortført eller skadet mens de forsøkte å livnære seg utenfor sikkerhetsperimetrene til Borno's garnisonbyer på grunn av begrensede jordbruksområder og få eller ingen levebrødsalternativer.' UNICEF's landrepresentant, Ms. Cristian Munduate, understreket det akutte behovet for handling. Hun sa: 'Hvert barn fortjener riktig ernæring og et liv fritt for sult. Det er ikke bare et ansvar, men en moralsk plikt for regjeringer og det globale samfunn å sikre at disse rettighetene blir opprettholdt.' David Stevenson, WFP's landrepresentant, fremhevet det langvarige problemet og sa: 'Hungerkrisen i Nigeria, drevet av den pågående konflikten i nordøst, må hastebehandles. Å gjenopprette fred i nordøst er kritisk for oss å bygge veier til produksjon og oppnå nordøstens potensiale som matlager for landet'. Trendanalyse for de nordøstlige delstatene indikerer konsekvent høye eller økende nivåer av matusikkerhet siden 2018. Over 4 millioner mennesker har årlig trengt presserende bistand siden juni 2020. FN oppfordrer Nigerias regjering, givere og interessenter til å binde ressurser og iverksette tiltak for å avverge en potensiell mat- og ernæringskatastrofe, og understreker behovet for umiddelbar støtte over hele nasjonen.

article_content: With the latest move, Beijing 'intends to blockade Taiwan' said an analyst. By RFA Staff 2023.11.09 -- Taiwanese authorities Thursday 'deployed appropriate forces' to respond to a transit by the Chinese aircraft carrier Shandong, the Ministry of National Defense (MOND) in Taipei said. 'PLAN Shandong Carrier Strike Group (CSG) has sailed north along the median line of the Taiwan Strait since yesterday afternoon,' said the MOND in a statement, referring to the Chinese Navy by its official name - the People's Liberation Army Navy (PLAN). 'Shandong CSG entered the waters north of Taiwan at around 0800 (UTC+8) today and is continuing to sail north. We have deployed appropriate forces to respond,' it said without giving further details. A carrier strike group normally consists of an aircraft carrier and several accompanying vessels, the number varies depending on the missions. One week ago, the U.S. 7th Fleet's USS Rafael Peralta and the Royal Canadian Navy's HMCS Ottawa made a similar Taiwan transit, which the U.S. Navy said was 'unremarkable, unprovocative, and consistent with international law.' The Shandong CSG has just conducted 'aggressive' drills in the western Pacific and entered the South China Sea on Nov. 6. With the latest transit, the PLAN 'intends to blockade Taiwan,' said Lin Ying-Yu, a Taiwanese defense analyst. 'The main message is: there is always at least one Chinese aircraft carrier somewhere near Taiwan, and that is the new normal,' he said. 'Given the current route, perhaps the Shandong is on its way to Dalian in Liaoning province for 'secret maintenance,' said Lin, Assistant Professor at Graduate Institute of International Affairs and Strategic Studies, Tamkang University. While the Taiwan military has a contingency plan in place to respond to such activities by the PLAN, the analyst says at the moment, its forces are 'just observing, monitoring the Chinese carrier's movements.' Intensive 'war-like' combat exercise The last time the Shandong transited the Taiwan Strait was in May. In September, right after another Taiwan transit by U.S. and Canadian warships, the Shandong also sailed past Taiwan but not through the strait. Shandong is China's first domestically built aircraft carrier, based on the Soviet Kuznetsov-class carrier and commissioned in December 2019. Prior to the Taiwan transit, the Shandong conducted an 'intensive war-like' combat exercise in the western Pacific, according to a statement by Japan's Ministry of Defense. During the nine-day exercise (Oct. 28 - Nov.5), it carried out around 420 jet fighter landings and 150 helicopter landings in the waters south of Japan's Miyako islands and east of the Philippines, the ministry said. That means about 63 aircraft sorties a day on average, nearly twice as many as when the Shandong CSG conducted its previous exercise in the region in April. Besides the aircraft carrier, two PLAN destroyers Guilin (164) and Changsha (173), and two frigates Xuchang (536) and Huangshan (570), also took part in the 'hostile' exercise. Between Nov. 4 and Nov. 7, the U.S Navy's Carl Vinson and Ronald Reagan carrier strike groups held joint drills with Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force's helicopter destroyer Hyuga, also in the Philippine Sea.

'PLAN Shandong Carrier Strike Group (CSG) har seilt nordover langs medianlinjen i Taiwansundet siden i går ettermiddag,' sa MOND i en erklæring, og refererte til den kinesiske marinen med dets offisielle navn - Folkets frigjøringshærs marine (PLAN). 'Shandong CSG kom inn i farvannet nord for Taiwan rundt kl 0800 (UTC+8) i dag og fortsetter å seile nordover. En hangarskipstridsgruppe består vanligvis av et hangarskip og flere medfølgende fartøy, antallet varierer avhengig av oppdragene. For en uke siden foretok den amerikanske 7. flåtes USS Rafael Peralta og den kongelige canadiske navys HMCS Ottawa en lignende transitt av Taiwan, som den amerikanske marinen beskrev som 'ikke bemerkelsesverdig, ikke provoserende og i samsvar med internasjonal lov.' Shandong CSG har nettopp gjennomført 'aggressive' øvelser i det vestlige Stillehavet og kom inn i Sør-Kina-havet den 6. november. Med den siste transitten 'har PLAN som mål å blokkere Taiwan,' sa Lin Ying-Yu, en taiwansk forsvarsanalytiker. 'Hovedbudskapet er: det er alltid minst ett kinesisk hangarskip et sted nær Taiwan, og det er den nye normalen,' sa han. 'Gitt den nåværende ruten, kanskje Shandong er på vei til Dalian i Liaoning-provinsen for 'hemmelig vedlikehold,' sa Lin, førsteamanuensis ved Graduate Institute of International Affairs and Strategic Studies, Tamkang University. Mens Taiwans militær har en beredskapsplan på plass for å reagere på slike aktiviteter fra PLAN, sier analytikeren at dets styrker for øyeblikket 'bare observerer, overvåker kinesiske hangarskipets bevegelser.' I september, rett etter en annen Taiwan-transitt av amerikanske og canadiske krigsskip, seilte Shandong også forbi Taiwan, men ikke gjennom sundet. Shandong er Kinas første innenlandsbygde hangarskip, basert på den sovjetiske Kuznetsov-klassen og tatt i bruk i desember 2019.
